title: Working with files & PDFs
summary: Read, write and parse files — text, CSV and PDFs — then feed extracted text to Claude for summaries and extraction.
objectives: Open, read and write files safely with the with statement
Choose the right mode and encoding for text files
Work with paths cleanly using pathlib
Read and write CSV data with the csv and pandas libraries
Extract text from PDFs using pypdf
Send extracted document text to Claude for summarisation and extraction
Handle missing files and bad input gracefully

quiz.q: Why prefer the with statement when opening a file?
options: It closes the file automatically, even on error
quiz.why: with open(...) as f: guarantees the file is closed when the block ends, even if an exception is raised.

quiz.q: Which file mode opens a file for writing and erases existing content?
quiz.why: "w" truncates (empties) the file before writing. Use "a" to append, "r" to read.

quiz.q: What encoding should you almost always specify when reading text files?
quiz.why: Passing encoding="utf-8" avoids garbled characters and platform-dependent defaults across Windows, macOS and Linux.

quiz.q: Which library reliably extracts text from a PDF in Python?
quiz.why: pypdf reads PDF pages and exposes extract_text(); pandas is for tables, requests for HTTP, json for JSON.

quiz.q: After extracting messy PDF text, how do you get a clean summary with Claude?
quiz.answer: Pass the extracted text inside the content of a messages.create call to the Claude Messages API.
quiz.why: You send the raw text as the user message content and ask Claude to summarise or extract fields; keep the API key in an env var.

quiz.q: True or false — pypdf's extract_text always returns perfectly clean, structured text.
quiz.why: False. Scanned or complex-layout PDFs often need cleaning, and image-only PDFs need OCR before any text is available.

body_markdown:
## Why files matter for your portfolio

Real projects live on data, and that data sits in **files**: text logs, CSV exports, JSON config, and a lot of **PDFs** — invoices, reports, contracts. A portfolio project that ingests a folder of documents and produces a clean summary looks far more impressive than another toy notebook.

In this lesson you'll read and write files safely, parse CSVs, pull text out of PDFs, and hand that text to Claude to summarise or extract structured fields.

## Opening files the safe way

Always use the `with` statement. It closes the file automatically when the block ends — even if an error is thrown. Specify the **mode** (`r` read, `w` write, `a` append) and the **encoding**.

```python
# Read a whole text file
with open("notes.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    text = f.read()

# Write a new file (overwrites!)
with open("out.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("Hello\n")
```

## Paths and CSVs

Use `pathlib` for paths so your code works on Windows, macOS and Linux. For tabular data, `pandas` reads and writes CSV in one line.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

data_dir = Path("data")
df = pd.read_csv(data_dir / "sales.csv")
print(df.head())
df.to_csv(data_dir / "clean.csv", index=False)
```

## Extracting text from PDFs

Install `pypdf`, loop over the pages, and call `extract_text()`. Note that PDFs are messy — text can arrive out of order, and scanned (image-only) PDFs return nothing until you run OCR.

```python
from pypdf import PdfReader

reader = PdfReader("report.pdf")
pages = [page.extract_text() or "" for page in reader.pages]
full_text = "\n".join(pages)
```

## Sending document text to Claude

Once you have the text, let an **A I** model do the reading. Send the extracted text as the message content and ask Claude to summarise or pull out fields. Keep your key in the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable.

```python
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic()
msg = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user",
               "content": "Summarise this report in 5 bullets:\n\n" + full_text}],
)
print(msg.content[0].text)
```

## Your task

Build a small script that reads every PDF in a `docs/` folder, extracts the text, and writes a one-paragraph Claude summary of each into a CSV.

slides.title: Open files safely
bullets: Always use the with statement.
It closes the file automatically.
Pick a mode: r read, w write, a append.
slides.code:
with open("notes.txt", "r",
          encoding="utf-8") as f:
    text = f.read()
slides.narration: The golden rule is to open files using the with statement. It guarantees the file is closed when the block ends, even if an error is thrown. You also choose a mode: r for read, w for write, and a for append. And always pass encoding equals U T F eight so your text doesn't come out garbled.

slides.title: Writing files
bullets: Mode w creates or overwrites a file.
Mode a adds to the end instead.
Remember newlines are not automatic.
slides.code:
with open("out.txt", "w",
          encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("Hello\n")
slides.narration: Writing is just as simple, but be careful: mode w overwrites the file completely, wiping whatever was there. If you want to add to a file instead, use mode a for append. And unlike print, write does not add a newline for you, so add the backslash n yourself when you need one.

slides.title: Paths with pathlib
bullets: pathlib works on Windows, Mac and Linux.
Join paths with the slash operator.
No more broken backslash strings.
slides.code:
from pathlib import Path
data = Path("data")
file = data / "sales.csv"
print(file.exists())
slides.narration: Hard-coding file paths as strings breaks the moment you move between Windows and Mac. The pathlib library fixes this. You make a Path object and join folders with the forward slash operator, and pathlib sorts out the right separator for you. It also gives handy methods like exists and is file.

slides.title: CSV with pandas
bullets: pandas reads a C S V in one line.
Inspect with head, write with to_csv.
Set index equals False when saving.
slides.code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("sales.csv")
print(df.head())
df.to_csv("clean.csv", index=False)
slides.narration: For tabular data, pandas is the fastest path. Read underscore c s v loads the whole table in one line, and head shows you the first few rows so you can sanity check it. When you save with to underscore c s v, pass index equals False, otherwise pandas writes an extra unnamed column of row numbers.

slides.title: Extract text from PDFs
bullets: Install and import pypdf.
Loop over pages, call extract_text.
Join the pages into one string.
slides.code:
from pypdf import PdfReader
r = PdfReader("report.pdf")
parts = [p.extract_text() or ""
         for p in r.pages]
text = "\n".join(parts)
slides.narration: Now the headline skill: pulling text out of P D Fs. Install pypdf, open the file with PdfReader, then loop over the pages and call extract underscore text on each. I add or empty string so a blank page never crashes the join. Finally we glue all the pages together into one big string ready to process.

slides.title: PDFs are messy
bullets: Text can arrive out of order.
Scanned PDFs return nothing without OCR.
Always clean before trusting the output.
slides.narration: A warning that saves hours: P D F text is rarely tidy. Columns can come out interleaved, spacing gets weird, and a scanned or photographed P D F is really just an image, so extract underscore text returns nothing until you run O C R, optical character recognition. Always eyeball the extracted text before you trust it downstream.

slides.title: Hand the text to Claude
bullets: Send extracted text as the message content.
Ask Claude to summarise or extract fields.
Keep the key in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
slides.code:
from anthropic import Anthropic
client = Anthropic()
msg = client.messages.create(
  model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
  max_tokens=1024,
  messages=[{"role":"user",
    "content":"Summarise:\n"+text}])
print(msg.content[0].text)
slides.narration: Here's where it gets powerful. Instead of writing brittle rules, let an A I read the document. We create an Anthropic client and call messages dot create with a model like claude sonnet four six. We put the extracted text into the content of the user message and ask Claude to summarise it. Keep your A P I key in the ANTHROPIC underscore A P I underscore KEY environment variable, never in your code.
